kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore adventures in Bolivia, Brazil and Ecuador"
lead: >-
  The adventurous appeal of combining Bolivia, Brazil and Ecuador lies in the changing style of travel: sightseeing at Iguazú and in Rio, a two-day 4×4 expedition across Bolivia's highlands and boat excursions in the Galápagos Islands. On the current 32-day journey through eight countries, the Bolivian section demands particular attention to altitude, while travellers in the Galápagos must choose between two island routes.
---

## Where the real adventure lies in this combination

**Bolivia, Brazil and Ecuador are included in one extended journey, but the demands of each country are very different.** The [Brazilian days](/brazil/) focus on Rio and Iguazú. The [Bolivian section](/bolivia/) includes 4×4 vehicles, high-altitude lagoons and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). [Ecuador](/ecuador/) adds historic Quito and a boat excursion around the Galápagos Islands. Calling all these experiences “extreme adventure” would be misleading: an off-road expedition at altitude, a walk along a tourist trail and a boat trip require very different preparation.

This selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The principal itinerary is [“Eight South American Countries in 32 Days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), also covering Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Peru and Colombia. **The three selected countries form part of the full itinerary; they do not constitute a ready-made, continuous journey limited to Bolivia, Brazil and Ecuador.** Travellers visit other countries between Brazil and Bolivia, and the Peru stages lie between Bolivia and Ecuador. For a geographical selection without the theme filter, see [all journeys involving these three countries](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_ecuador/).

## Brazil: accessible panoramas rather than demanding trekking

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the programme includes a trip up Corcovado to Christ the Redeemer and an excursion to Sugarloaf Mountain. Sugarloaf is reached by cable car, with a stop at Morro da Urca; travellers see [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/) as part of the Corcovado excursion. These activities offer panoramic views and an introduction to Rio's terrain, but **technical climbing and a multi-day hiking route are not included in the programme**.

The next stop is [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) for an excursion to the Brazilian side of the falls. The main experiences here are walking along visitor paths, humid air and powerful cascades. The Macuco Safari is available separately at an additional cost; it is not automatically included in the standard adventure programme. Check the distinction between viewing platforms and an independent active excursion before choosing the tour.

Travellers looking for more sporting activities can explore [adventure tours featuring Brazil](/interests/adventure/tours/brazil/), which may offer different destinations and activities. Those experiences should not, however, be attributed to this specific 32-day tour unless they are confirmed.

## Bolivia: a two-day high-altitude 4×4 journey

The most pronounced adventure section of this combination is in Bolivia. After stopping in San Pedro de Atacama in Chile, the group heads to the border and transfers to 4×4 vehicles. Over two days, the route visits Laguna Verde, the Dalí Desert, the Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geysers, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), other mountain lagoons and salt flats. The final stops include [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), Colchani and Incahuasi Island.

This is a [two-day jeep excursion with an English-speaking guide](/bolivia/uyuni/uyuni-salt-flats-4x4-tour-2-days/), not a hiking trek. An overnight stay in an expedition-style desert hotel is included. **Part of the route runs above 4,000 metres**, so the main challenges are altitude, long drives, cold, wind and the possibility of altitude sickness. Judging the difficulty by walking distance alone would be pointless.

The itinerary includes a stop in San Pedro de Atacama before crossing into Bolivia to allow for acclimatisation. Such a stop does not guarantee that altitude symptoms will be avoided. Travellers with chronic medical conditions, a history of altitude sickness or uncertain altitude tolerance should discuss the journey with a doctor beforehand and inform the organiser about any significant limitations.

After [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), the itinerary includes a flight to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), with a city tour and a visit to the Valley of the Moon. The route then travels via Tiwanaku into Peru. This marks a transition from a high-altitude nature expedition to a cultural programme, rather than a continuation of the active 4×4 safari.

## Ecuador: the Galápagos boat excursion

The Ecuador section begins in [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), visiting the historic centre and the equator. Travellers then fly to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/): from Baltra Airport they transfer to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), exploring the island's highlands and lava tunnels.

The following day features a boat excursion with **one of two alternatives**. The first visits North Seymour Island and Bachas Beach, with a landing and an opportunity to snorkel. The second visits South Plaza and Cape Carrión. One confirmed route is included after booking; both are not promised together. Even a short boat trip depends on weather, sea conditions and the rules governing visits to the islands.

The [North Seymour excursion](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/north-seymour-island-tour/) and the [South Plaza trip](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/south-plaza-island-tour/) differ in geography, landing arrangements and wildlife. Active travellers should check where walking is permitted and where viewing is only possible from the boat. Snorkelling on one route **does not mean scuba diving** or that diving equipment is included.

## Combining high altitude, the tropics and island waters

| Section | Main challenge |
|---|---|
| Rio and Iguazú | Heat, humidity and walking |
| Bolivian lagoons | Altitude, cold and 4×4 travel |
| Santa Cruz | Walks and transfers |
| Galápagos Islands | Sea conditions, boarding and weather |

Pack for the most contrasting days. At Iguazú, waterproof protection and shoes with reliable grip are useful; in Bolivia, warm layers and protection against sun and wind; on marine excursions, waterproof protection for belongings and clothes suitable for boarding a boat. Clothing intended only for hot Brazil is insufficient for the conditions of Bolivia's highlands.

The 32-day programme includes flights and overland transfers between these countries, as well as other parts of South America. Plan for the entire chain, allowing time for borders, acclimatisation, connections and recovery. You cannot simply arrange the three countries next to each other on a map and expect the same itinerary. Ada Tours helps organise the sequence, coordinate overland transfers and included excursions, and assess appropriate activity levels for a particular group.

Entry requirements must be checked for each traveller's nationality **across the full actual itinerary**, including transit countries. Payment options also differ: do not assume that the same card will work, or the same currency will be accepted, throughout Brazil, Bolivia and Ecuador. Protected-area access, current Galápagos National Park rules and the excursion boat's conditions must be confirmed for the chosen dates.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Who this itinerary suits

This trip suits travellers who enjoy **changing natural environments and modes of transport**: a coastal city, waterfalls, rugged highlands and island seas. It requires tolerance for frequent travel and a willingness to adapt to the weather. The Bolivian 4×4 section is particularly relevant when assessing physical demands; the Galápagos section when assessing sea conditions and choosing the confirmed excursion. For similar options, compare [multi-country adventure itineraries](/multi-country/interests/adventure/) and the [general collection of adventure journeys](/interests/adventure/).

## Frequently asked questions about adventures in Bolivia, Brazil and Ecuador

### Is a mountain climb in Rio included?

No. On the featured [32-day tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), Corcovado and Sugarloaf are visited on sightseeing excursions using the specified transport. Technical climbing is not part of the programme.

### How demanding is the Bolivian section?

The main difficulties are high altitude and long 4×4 drives. Some sections run above 4,000 metres, with an overnight stay in an expedition hotel. Physical demands and acclimatisation must be assessed individually; the [two-day Uyuni route](/bolivia/uyuni/uyuni-salt-flats-4x4-tour-2-days/) should not be mistaken for a typical city excursion.

### Can North Seymour and South Plaza be visited in a single day?

No. They are alternative Galápagos options in the current itinerary, and one is confirmed after booking. Landing arrangements, snorkelling opportunities and applicable restrictions are agreed for the selected route.

buttonLabel: "Explore the history of Bolivia, Brazil and Ecuador"
lead: >-
  A cultural journey through Bolivia, Brazil and Ecuador reveals three distinct stories: the architecture and urban life of Rio de Janeiro, the pre-Columbian ceremonial centre of Tiwanaku, and historic Quito with its churches and colonial art school. On the current 32-day itinerary, they are separated by other countries and nature-based stages, so the time devoted to heritage sites should be judged by the actual excursion days.
---

## The historical eras connecting these three countries

A journey through [Brazil](/brazil/), [Bolivia](/bolivia/) and [Ecuador](/ecuador/) offers a chance to compare the urban architecture of coastal Brazil, Andean highland civilisations and the colonial art of Ecuador's capital. The comparison is meaningful only when the route actually includes particular monuments and excursions, rather than merely passing through these countries.

This selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Its foundation is a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Brazil comes early in the journey, Bolivia after Chile's Atacama, and Ecuador after Peru. **There is no separate ready-made three-country itinerary with direct connections from Brazil to Bolivia to Ecuador in this selection.** For geography regardless of interest, consult the [three-country catalogue](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_ecuador/).

## Rio de Janeiro: architecture against an Atlantic backdrop

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), two excursions with a Russian-speaking guide are included: Corcovado and the Christ the Redeemer statue, and Sugarloaf Mountain with a visit to the historic neighbourhoods. In the city centre, travellers discover old church architecture, monasteries, the main cathedral and colonial buildings.

Rio is fascinating for the way its architecture and landscape come together. Corcovado offers views over the bay and the city, while [Sugarloaf Mountain](/brazil/place/sugarloaf-mountain/) overlooks neighbourhoods by the ocean. It makes a strong first stage of a cultural trip: visitors can see how the city developed between the sea and steep hillsides. The viewing platforms and cable car themselves, however, are panoramic experiences rather than an exploration of an ancient civilisation.

The next Brazilian destination is [Iguazú Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). It is an important stop on the full itinerary, but its focus is nature. The fact that a tour has an overall cultural theme does not mean that every stop in Brazil is historical. Compare [culture and history tours in Brazil](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/brazil/) according to the city excursions actually included.

## Bolivia: Tiwanaku and the traditions of La Paz

The Bolivian journey begins with a high-altitude nature section through lagoons and Uyuni, before continuing to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). On a city tour, travellers visit historic districts, the Witches' Market and the [Valley of the Moon](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/). The market offers an insight into living urban culture and traditions, while the Valley of the Moon, with its unusual terrain, is the day's nature stop.

Bolivia's main stand-alone historical site on this itinerary is [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), an ancient ceremonial centre on the Altiplano. The tour includes the Gate of the Sun and the Kalasasaya Temple. According to UNESCO, Tiwanaku was the political and spiritual centre of a distinct pre-Columbian civilisation that flourished long before European colonisation. Its stone architecture reveals the historical depth of the Andes, which cannot be understood by looking only at modern La Paz.

The [excursion from La Paz via Tiwanaku to Desaguadero](/bolivia/la-paz/tiwanaku-desaguadero-from-la-paz/) is combined with the crossing into Peru. Allow adequate time to explore the archaeological site: the drive and border procedures take place on the same day. Tiwanaku is at high altitude, and the preceding stages include sections above 4,000 metres, so health and acclimatisation matter even on a historical excursion. If Bolivia is your main cultural priority, explore [journeys through its historic sites](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/bolivia/).

## Ecuador: Quito, Baroque art and the equator

After the Peruvian section, travellers reach [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/). The itinerary describes a sightseeing day in the historic centre, with its churches and squares, together with a visit to the equator area. Quito's colonial architecture is distinguished by a local school of art that brought together European traditions and the work of Indigenous artists. The historic centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

On the [Quito and equator excursion](/ecuador/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/quito-panecillo-and-equator/), travellers explore the old city, its religious art and urban legends. Another part of the trip visits Mitad del Mundo and the Intiñan Museum: this introduces geography, the history of measurement and the tourist interpretation of the equator rather than an archaeological site comparable to Tiwanaku.

**The heritage sites of Bolivia and Ecuador belong to different historical and cultural periods.** [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) represents an ancient Andean civilisation, while central Quito is particularly notable for its surviving colonial-era buildings. Calling them “two Inca cities” would be inaccurate. Other trips with a cultural programme in Ecuador can be found in the [country's thematic catalogue](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/ecuador/).

After Quito, the journey continues to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The excursions there focus primarily on nature and wildlife. Even though the islands make up a substantial part of the journey, they do not replace time spent studying Quito's architecture and museums.

## The practical choices for travellers

| Historical focus | Where to find it |
|---|---|
| City and churches by the ocean | Rio de Janeiro |
| The pre-Columbian Andes | Tiwanaku |
| Colonial art | Historic Quito |
| Living urban traditions | La Paz |

For ancient history, Tiwanaku will be the key stop. Quito and the Rio city tour offer the richest encounters with colonial architecture. To experience contemporary Andean urban life, pay particular attention to La Paz. All three themes appear on the same 32-day journey, but visits to specific museums, religious sites or optional excursions depend on the day's programme.

To compare other history-and-culture combinations, browse the [multi-country cultural trips catalogue](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/) and the [Culture and History section](/interests/culture-and-history/). If you want a tailor-made journey covering only these three countries, Ada Tours can discuss a separate route, but flight and accommodation arrangements would need to change.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Combining sightseeing with climate and transfers

Rio is warm and humid; La Paz and Tiwanaku are affected by high altitude; and Quito also lies in the Andes. City and heritage walks call for comfortable footwear, protection against sun and rain, and warm layers for the highlands. Even when temples and museums are the focus, the effects of altitude cannot be ignored after successive flights and road journeys.

The full tour travels through Peru between Bolivia and Ecuador, so time at historical sites is distributed across the real 32-day schedule. Shortening the journey changes both the number of cities and the ability to visit monuments without rushing. Ada Tours helps establish priorities, coordinate the order of excursions and transfers, and allow a sensible amount of travel time.

Entry and transit requirements must be checked for the travellers' nationalities **across all countries on the actual itinerary**. Brazil, Bolivia and Ecuador have different national monetary systems; card acceptance, currency exchange and the use of cash should be checked before departure. Museum opening hours and access to religious buildings must also be confirmed for the travel dates rather than assumed from general descriptions.

## Frequently asked questions about a historical journey through Bolivia, Brazil and Ecuador

### How does Tiwanaku differ from Quito's historic centre?

[Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) is an archaeological centre of a distinct ancient Andean civilisation. [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) preserves extensive colonial architecture and is known for its local Baroque art tradition. Together, they reveal different periods in the continent's history.

### Is there a separate three-country cultural tour without other countries?

This selection offers a [32-day route through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). A trip limited to Brazil, Bolivia and Ecuador would need to be designed and agreed separately, rather than simply dropping neighbouring days from the programme.

### Can the Galápagos be skipped to spend more time in museums?

Such a change can be discussed when arranging a tailor-made itinerary. On the existing tour, the [Galápagos](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) are already included as a nature section. Island excursions are not automatically exchanged for additional museum visits.

## Nature in Brazil, Bolivia and Ecuador: waterfalls, salt flats and islands

This combination is compelling for its progression from humid waterfalls to dry highlands and then volcanic islands. All three countries feature in the [Ada Tours 32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). **A selection of three countries does not mean a separate short itinerary**: between Brazil and Bolivia, the tour visits Argentina, Uruguay and Chile, and between Bolivia and Ecuador it visits Peru.

For nature-focused travel, it makes sense to compare the actual days spent on excursions. At [Iguazú Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the programme includes a visit to the Brazilian side with a Russian-speaking guide. Bolivia offers a two-day journey in 4×4 vehicles. In the Galápagos, the itinerary includes Santa Cruz and one of two alternative boat excursions.

## Which natural sites are visited, and where?

| Country | Main natural attractions |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Iguazú and tropical rainforest |
| Bolivia | Lagoons, geysers and Uyuni |
| Ecuador | Santa Cruz and the Galápagos |

### Brazil: the main nature day at Iguazú

After [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), travellers fly to Foz do Iguaçu. The Brazilian side offers sweeping views of the waterfall system and river cascades surrounded by forest. This is the Brazilian section's main nature experience. In Rio, the route also passes through Tijuca Forest on the way to Corcovado, but it does not include a separate forest expedition.

**The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are optional extras at an additional cost.** Travellers hoping to watch birds or take a boat ride should arrange the appropriate option when agreeing the itinerary. Photos of those activities are not evidence that they are included in the tour price. Other possibilities appear in the [selection of nature tours in Brazil](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/).

### Bolivia: colourful lagoons and Uyuni by jeep

From San Pedro de Atacama, the route crosses the border and continues in 4×4 vehicles to [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), Licancabur Volcano, the Polques hot springs and the Sol de Mañana geysers. The same day includes [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), where flamingos may be seen. The overnight stay is in an expedition-style hotel.

The next day brings smaller lagoons, Ollagüe Volcano, the Chiguana Salt Flat and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), followed by Colchani and Incahuasi Island. **The mirror-like surface of Uyuni depends on the presence of water**: in dry conditions, it is a vast white salt plain; in wet conditions, a reflective landscape. Weather and natural effects should never be guaranteed on the basis of a photograph.

This is a vehicle-based expedition with sightseeing stops, not a multi-day hiking trip. Nevertheless, sections of the route rise above 4,000 metres, so the main challenges are altitude, cold and road travel.

### Ecuador: the nature of Santa Cruz and a choice of boat route

After Quito, the group flies to Baltra and transfers to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The programme includes the island's [highlands](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-highlands/) and lava tunnels, followed by accommodation in Puerto Ayora. The contrast between drier northern areas and greener parts of the island is already visible during the transfer.

The boat excursion in the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) has **two mutually exclusive alternatives**. One possible route visits [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas Beach for seabird watching and snorkelling. The alternative visits South Plaza and Cape Carrión, featuring coastal habitats, iguanas and sea lions. The specific option is confirmed after booking; the programme does not promise both routes in a single included day.

## Comparing three natural environments

Iguazú means walking near powerful water at relatively low elevations; Bolivia means cold high-altitude roads and mineral-rich lakes; the Galápagos mean boats, island trails and protected visitor sites. These experiences complement one another but require different preparation.

For Iguazú, pack a waterproof layer and non-slip shoes. For Bolivia's Altiplano, bring warm clothing and protection from sun and wind. For the islands, lightweight UV-protective clothing, suitable items for a boat trip and adherence to protected-area rules are important. Sightings of particular animals depend on natural conditions and the excursion.

Altitude preparation deserves special attention. A stop in San Pedro de Atacama is scheduled before Bolivia, but it does not rule out altitude sickness: the rate of ascent matters even for fit travellers. Individual risks, especially those involving heart or lung conditions, should be discussed with a doctor before confirming the programme.

## Choosing the itinerary and planning transfers

The [Bolivia, Brazil and Ecuador selection](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_ecuador/) displays tours that include these countries, while [all multi-country nature journeys](/multi-country/interests/nature/) help you find other combinations. If you want a holiday limited to the named three countries, Ada Tours can discuss a tailor-made sequence and package of services. Flights and duration would have to be calculated again: neighbouring countries cannot simply be deleted from the eight-country programme without altering the journey.

Entry, transit and health requirements must be checked for the traveller's nationality and the countries where transfers actually take place. The same applies to payment options, baggage and protected-area access rules. These arrangements must cover the full journey, not just the three country names in the catalogue title.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Bolivia, Brazil and Ecuador

### Can all three countries be visited on one short trip?

That would require a separate tailor-made itinerary. Our current journey covers eight countries, with its nature stops distributed among other days and flights.

### Are the Bird Park and Macuco Safari included?

No. These are optional services on the Brazilian side of Iguazú. The excursion to the waterfalls is included in the standard programme.

### Is the mirror effect at Uyuni guaranteed?

No. It depends on the salt flat's conditions and the presence of water. A dry salt surface offers a different, equally characteristic landscape.

### Can both Galápagos alternatives be visited?

The tour includes one of two marine excursions. The specific route is confirmed after booking.

## Three natural worlds on one extended journey

**What makes Brazil, Bolivia and Ecuador appealing is the change in ecosystems, not the number of countries.** In [Brazil's Iguazú region](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), enormous waterfalls meet the humid Atlantic Forest. On the [Bolivian Altiplano](/bolivia/), open lagoons attract flamingos and other high-altitude birds. The [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) in Ecuador are known for animals adapted to life on a volcanic archipelago and in the surrounding ocean.

This selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. It is based on a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Alongside Brazil, Bolivia and Ecuador, the tour visits Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Peru and Colombia. The countries shown in the filter are parts of a larger route: the group does not travel directly from Iguazú to Bolivia's lagoons and then fly immediately to the Galápagos. Encounters with flamingos and Galápagos animals support the “Wildlife and Safaris” theme, while the waterfalls, lagoons and salt flats also belong to the separate “Nature” theme. Other options with the same geography appear in the [Bolivia–Brazil–Ecuador selection](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_ecuador/).

## Brazil: waterfalls and the Atlantic Forest at Iguazú

In Brazil, the nature section centres on [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The programme includes a group tour of the Brazilian side of the falls with a Russian-speaking guide. The walk introduces visitors to the cascades, surrounding vegetation and humid forest protected by national parks along the Argentine border.

UNESCO's World Heritage description identifies this area with the Atlantic Forest and its rich plant and animal diversity. But **the presence of a species in a national park does not mean it will appear beside a visitor trail**. The principal experience is the cascades themselves, the spray and the forest views; the standard itinerary does not include tracking jaguars, tapirs or rare birds.

The [Bird Park](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) and Macuco Safari are offered as optional extras on the current tour. Both must be arranged and paid for separately. The Bird Park provides a managed setting in which to encounter birds, which differs from observing wildlife freely in the forest. The [Iguazú excursion](/brazil/foz-do-iguacu/iguazu-brazil-group-russian-program/) has its own confirmed inclusions, and optional activities are not automatically added.

The Brazilian days also begin with [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/), but the programme focuses primarily on viewpoints and architecture there. For other wildlife experiences, compare [tours featuring Brazil under “Wildlife and Safaris”](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/), checking which country actually hosts each wildlife-watching day: on a multi-country route it may be outside Brazil. For waterfalls and forest scenery, explore [nature tours featuring Brazil](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/).

## Bolivia: flamingos, colourful lagoons and salt flats

The Bolivian section begins after Chile's Atacama. Two days of 4×4 travel take in Laguna Verde, the Dalí Desert, the Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geysers and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Flamingos associated with the high-altitude lakes are specifically mentioned in the programme. The following day, travellers see more lagoons before continuing towards the [Uyuni Salt Flats](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

**Unlike Iguazú, this landscape has very little forest vegetation: the natural spectacle unfolds across an open plateau.** The water's colour and salt-encrusted shores create distinctive photographic conditions. Watching birds depends on the distance to a colony, lighting, weather and the possibility of stopping safely at the right place. Birds choose where to gather, so neither an exact number of encounters nor a photograph of a particular species can be promised.

The [two-day Uyuni 4×4 excursion](/bolivia/uyuni/uyuni-salt-flats-4x4-tour-2-days/) includes an English-speaking guide and an overnight stay in an expedition hotel. Some sections exceed 4,000 metres. Safety is particularly important here: high altitude, cold and possible altitude sickness affect the pace that is realistic. Stops for birdwatching must remain within the confirmed route, not wherever leaving the permitted road would be necessary. For a more detailed experience in this region, explore [tours featuring Bolivia under “Wildlife and Safaris”](/interests/wildlife/tours/bolivia/).

## Ecuador: giant tortoises on Santa Cruz

After the Peruvian section, the group reaches Quito and then flies to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). From Baltra Airport, travellers transfer to [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). The itinerary includes an [excursion to the Santa Cruz highlands and lava tunnels](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-lava-tunnels/), where giant tortoises in the island's natural setting are a particular highlight.

Santa Cruz offers a completely different nature experience from Bolivia: green highland areas on a volcanic island, local vegetation and tortoises. This is neither a dry Andean plateau nor the forest surrounding the falls. Walk at an unhurried pace, stay on designated paths and keep a respectful distance from animals. Sightings of individual tortoises depend on the day's conditions, even in an area known for them.

For visitors interested in natural parks, the deciding factor is not a promise to “see every species” but the choice of the right excursions. The Galápagos are governed by a special conservation regime, with access to particular sites regulated. Routes and current rules should be checked before departure.

## The Galápagos: two different options for a day at sea

The next day involves a trip to neighbouring islands. The [current tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes **one of two alternative excursions**, with the final option confirmed after booking:

- [North Seymour and Bachas Beach](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/north-seymour-island-tour/). The excursion description mentions frigatebirds, blue-footed boobies, sea lions and other seabirds. After exploring the island, there may be a stop by a lagoon and snorkelling at Bachas Beach.
- [South Plaza and Cape Carrión](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/south-plaza-island-tour/). This itinerary includes walking among sea lions and land iguanas, birdwatching and snorkelling near Cape Carrión, where rays and tropical fish may be encountered.

**These are alternatives, not two included days.** Travellers cannot be promised both bird photography on Seymour and a walk on South Plaza within a single confirmed boat excursion. The presence of animals in the habitat description does not guarantee an encounter, while underwater sightings depend on water clarity, weather and compliance with the rules.

The choice should be based on the type of landscape, the specific walking programme and how passengers board the vessel. Sea conditions may change on either route. If seeing a particular bird or animal is essential, discuss the itinerary in advance rather than promising the sighting. [Ecuador tours in “Wildlife and Safaris”](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/) offer other combinations of island and mainland stops.

## Weather, altitude and respectful wildlife watching

At Iguazú, bring quick-drying clothing, comfortable non-slip shoes and waterproof protection for equipment. On Bolivia's Altiplano, warm layers, wind and sun protection, and an individual assessment of altitude tolerance are essential. In the Galápagos, a hat, protection for belongings against seawater and footwear suitable for permitted paths and landings are useful.

Ada Tours helps coordinate flights, overland transfers, excursion days and time available for wildlife observation. ## Frequently asked questions about wildlife in Bolivia, Brazil and Ecuador

### Can flamingos and giant tortoises be seen on the same journey?

Yes. The route includes the [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) area, where flamingos occur, and [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), where the programme features giant tortoises. ### Are both Galápagos island routes included?

No. One boat-excursion day is included: either [North Seymour](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/north-seymour-island-tour/) or [South Plaza](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/south-plaza-island-tour/). The choice is confirmed after booking, and both island alternatives are not promised together.

### Does the trip guarantee wildlife sightings at Iguazú?

No. [Brazil's Iguazú](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) is known for its biodiversity, but the standard group excursion focuses on the falls. The Bird Park is an optional extra; walking through the national park does not amount to an organised search for particular animals.

## Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador and Peru: what connects the four countries?

In [Brazil](/brazil/), the journey begins in São Paulo, [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and on the Brazilian side of Iguazú. The Bolivian section includes high-altitude lagoons, a 4×4 expedition to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), La Paz and Tiwanaku. In [Peru](/peru/), the route continues to Lake Titicaca, Cusco, [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Lima. In [Ecuador](/ecuador/), travellers visit Quito followed by the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/).

**These destinations appear on the current 32-day tour, but between Brazil and Bolivia the itinerary also travels through Argentina, Uruguay and Chile.** After Ecuador, it continues into Colombia. The four selected countries are a filter applied to the main countries of a larger programme, not a promise of a direct Brazil–Bolivia transfer or an end to the journey in Guayaquil.

Our catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} involving all four countries. Compare this selection with the complete order of the [eight-country South American itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) and the conditions of each excursion.

## Brazil: coastal cities and Iguazú's cascades before the highlands

In Rio de Janeiro, the programme includes Corcovado and the Christ the Redeemer statue, as well as Sugarloaf Mountain, followed by a domestic flight to Iguazú Falls. Travellers explore the Brazilian side of the falls; the Bird Park is offered separately from the main excursion. The next stage visits the Argentine side of Iguazú and continues to Buenos Aires.

The Brazilian section is much lower in elevation than the Andean regions travellers will encounter later. Rio typically has warm, humid weather, but that is no reason to pack only for the tropics: the roads through Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons are still ahead. Comfortable layers and sun protection are needed for different stages, rather than a single season across the whole continent.

If your priority is cities and waterfalls alone, compare [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) with the much longer journey across the Andes.

## Bolivia: 4×4 vehicles, lagoons and Uyuni

The high-altitude stage begins after San Pedro de Atacama in Chile. Travellers cross the Bolivian border for a **two-day 4×4 journey** accompanied by an English-speaking guide. The listed attractions include colourful lagoons, the Sol de Mañana geysers, the Polques hot springs, volcanic landscapes, the Chiguana Salt Flat and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). A flight to La Paz follows.

The main difference from an urban sightseeing tour is the long-distance travel at altitude and more basic road conditions. Even with organised transport, this section can be physically demanding. Discuss altitude tolerance, nighttime temperatures, meals and the schedule of stops in advance. The presence of hot springs along the route does not automatically mean that a separate SPA package is included.

After La Paz, the route goes via Tiwanaku to the border with Peru near Desaguadero. This is a genuine overland connection between the two countries, which should be considered when checking travel documents and border-crossing time.

## Peru: from Titicaca to Machu Picchu and the coast

The first major stops in Peru are Puno and Lake Titicaca, including an excursion to the Uros Islands. The group then travels to Cusco on a dedicated tourist bus. [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) has its own sightseeing day with an English-speaking guide, followed by cultural landmarks in Cusco and a flight to Lima.

Seasonal planning for Bolivia and Peru should follow **the high-altitude route**, rather than a general idea of “summer in South America”. Conditions on the salt flats and at Machu Picchu can differ even within the same week: rainfall, elevation, road access and protected-site entry rules all matter. Precise train schedules, tickets and excursion time slots must be checked for the actual dates.

Lima offers a change of setting: after mountain roads, travellers reach a coastal city, from which our itinerary includes a flight to Quito. Those with limited time can compare [Peru programmes](/peru/tour/) to decide whether adding the Galápagos is worthwhile.

## Ecuador: Quito, the Galápagos and special island visitor procedures

From Lima, travellers fly to Quito. The itinerary includes a tour of Quito and the equator, then a flight to the Galápagos via Baltra and accommodation in the Santa Cruz Island area. The next excursion day includes **one of two alternatives**: North Seymour and Bachas Beach, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. Both options are not promised on the same itinerary. After the islands, the group departs via Guayaquil.

The Galápagos have special conservation measures: visitor transit controls, baggage biosecurity screening and protected-area fees. Their current amounts, application procedures and inclusion in the quoted price must be checked before booking. The rules for a routine domestic flight in mainland Ecuador cannot simply be assumed to apply to the archipelago. Ada Tours coordinates flights, the chosen island excursion and sufficient time for these formalities.

The islands are known for endemic animals, but seeing a particular species on a specific day depends on the location and natural conditions. Base your choice on the confirmed marine-excursion itinerary, rather than a list of every species found across the Galápagos.

## Money, climate and documents for the complete journey

Brazil uses the real, Bolivia the boliviano, Peru the sol and Ecuador the US dollar as its official currency. These are four distinct payment situations. Decide in advance which expenses are included and where local funds will be needed; acceptance of a card issued by a particular bank and of cash US dollars at individual businesses must be confirmed separately. The currency in which the tour is billed should not automatically be treated as the means of payment at every stop.

Document checks depend on nationality, passport type and the entire sequence of borders. For the 32-day tour discussed here, that also includes Argentina, Uruguay, Chile and Colombia. The overland Chile–Bolivia and Bolivia–Peru crossings, international flights and the separate Galápagos rules are especially important. Medical requirements and insurance should be confirmed for the route and dates; altitude tolerance is best discussed individually.

If waterfalls, the Andes, Inca heritage and the Galápagos are your main interests, while the other countries matter less, we can discuss a different sequence and a new quotation. The terms of the extended journey do not automatically carry over to a shorter option.

## Frequently asked questions about Brazil, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador

### Does the current itinerary travel directly from Brazil to Bolivia?

No. The published tour visits Argentina, Uruguay and Chile between those stages. The Bolivian 4×4 route starts after San Pedro de Atacama.

### Why should altitude be discussed before travelling to Uyuni?

Because the route includes high-altitude lagoons and 4×4 roads, then continues through La Paz and Lake Titicaca. Demands and altitude tolerance vary by person, so the pace of the entire section needs to be planned.

### Can both Galápagos island-excursion options be experienced?

The published programme includes **one** of two alternative boat routes. The specific excursion is confirmed at booking, subject to availability and current conditions.

### Is a separate document required for the Galápagos Islands?

The archipelago has a distinct visitor transit-control and baggage-biosecurity procedure. Check the current process, any applicable fees and required documentation before the trip.

### Can Ecuador be treated as the end of this tour?

No. The current 32-day journey continues to excursions in Colombia after Ecuador. Ending in Guayaquil would require separate changes to the return tickets and the programme.
